english: Let $x_{0}=0$ and, for every integer $n\ge0$, let $x_{n+1}=\dfrac{4x_{n}+3\sqrt{1-x_{n}^{2}}}{5}$. Then the value of $x_{100}$ is ______.
solution: So $\theta_{n+1}=\sin^{-1}x_{n}+\sin^{-1}\dfrac35$ if this is $\le\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, and $\pi-\left(\theta_{n}+\varphi\right)$ otherwise
solution_full: Each $x_{n}$ lies in $[-1,1]$ (shown below), so let $\theta_{n}=\sin^{-1}x_{n}\in\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$; then $\sqrt{1-x_{n}^{2}}=\cos\theta_{n}\ge0$. Let $\varphi=\sin^{-1}\dfrac35$, so $\cos\varphi=\dfrac45$.

Addition of inverse sines: $\theta_{n+1}=\sin^{-1}\sin(\theta_{n}+\varphi)$, which equals $\theta_{n}+\varphi$ when $\theta_{n}+\varphi\le\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $\pi-(\theta_{n}+\varphi)$ when $\dfrac{\pi}{2}<\theta_{n}+\varphi\le\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$. (This is the rule $\sin^{-1}a+\sin^{-1}b=\pi-\sin^{-1}\left(a\sqrt{1-b^{2}}+b\sqrt{1-a^{2}}\right)$ when $a,b>0$ and $a^{2}+b^{2}>1$.)
Since $\tan\varphi=\dfrac34$, we have $\varphi<\dfrac{\pi}{4}$, and $\tan2\varphi=\dfrac{24}{7}>\sqrt3$ gives $2\varphi>\dfrac{\pi}{3}$, so $3\varphi>\dfrac{\pi}{2}$. Also $2\varphi<\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.
Hence from $n=2$ the sequence of angles alternates $2\varphi,\ \pi-3\varphi,\ 2\varphi,\ldots$, and $\theta_{n}=2\varphi$ for every even $n\ge2$.
originality_note: New: an algebraic recurrence that is secretly the rotation theta -> theta + sin^-1(3/5) folded back into [-pi/2, pi/2] by the principal range of sin^-1; after two steps the fold makes the orbit 2-periodic, so x_100 = sin 2phi (way 1). Closest known: evaluating sin(sin^-1 a + sin^-1 b) or the rule for sin^-1 a + sin^-1 b when a^2 + b^2 > 1. Different because: the rule is applied repeatedly and the branch switch produces the period.

concept_use.Addition and subtractions of angles invo: theta_(n+1) = sin^-1 x_n + sin^-1(3/5), or pi minus it when the sum exceeds pi/2 (the a^2 + b^2 > 1 case), drives the iteration.
concept_use.Compound angles: sin(A+/-B), cos(A+/-B),: The recurrence is sin theta cos phi + cos theta sin phi = sin(theta + phi), and x_100 = sin 2phi = 24/25.

stem_review: Read as a student: every function has a stated domain, every symbol is introduced before use, principal values are stated, every condition is given, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed with mpmath/numpy and is unique and equal to the Answer Plan; no hyperbolic functions or asymptotes. Checked that the square root is always real (x_n is a sine), computed the first 100 terms with 40-digit precision (period 0.96, 0.936 from n = 2), and that 0.96 is a decimal between 0 and 1. The first design of this row (sin^-1 x - cos^-1 x = sin^-1((x-2)/5)) was dropped after the web check found a published equation of the same form. Changed: question redesigned before writing.
key_step: Recognising the recurrence as sin(theta_n + phi) with sin phi = 3/5 and following the principal-range fold to a 2-cycle.
justification: The compound-angle reading of the recurrence is the key idea, then a branch analysis of an iteration; numerical answer. Two ideas linked; comparable to 2021-P1-Q15 (L3) ITF statements with telescoping and to 2025-P2-Q3 (L3).
